title: Opening the black box of the living eye
text: Hi, I'm Varun, and this video is about turning a living optic nerve into data a machine can read. Before you can teach a machine to spot glaucoma, you have to answer a harder question first. text: Technology that finally cracked it open. A nerve becomes data when you measure its thickness. OCT reads the layer beneath the surface micron by micron, and that map is what our whole project runs on. The first glimpse came around

title: What is Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT)?
text: 1850 when the physicist Hermann von Helmholtz built the ophthalmoscope, light and mirrors that let a doctor see the living optic nerve for the first time. Within a few years, surgeons spotted glaucoma's fingerprint, the center of the nerve head hollowed out, cupped like a crater. But a picture of the surface isn't enough. title: Measuring the retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL)
text: Layer, a sheet of nerve cables microns thick. To fight it, you must measure that layer. That's what optical coherence tomography does. It fires a beam of light into the eye and reads the faint echoes from each retinal layer, timing them against a reference beam. title: The Harvard GDP dataset and the "small data" bottleneck
text: Nerve tissue survives point by point across the eye. That map is our raw material, and specifically we built on the Harvard Glaucoma Detection and Progression Data Set, Harvard GDP, released by the Harvard Ophthalmology AI Lab, 1,000 patients each with an OCT nerve fiber map made public for researchers. A thousand real eyes turned into data. 1,000 though is a tiny number in the world of deep learning. Models that recognize everyday objects train on millions of examples, and that limitation shaped everything we did next. Your turn, paste this. A thousand labeled examples sounds like a lot. Explain why it's almost nothing to a modern AI, and what specifically goes wrong when a deep network trains on too few labels. Ask for the failure mode by name, not just the word overfitting. If the answer doesn't tell you what the model learns instead of the real signal, push back. Turning a nerve into data with barely any labels to learn from, we had to teach a model to teach itself.
